subject.title: [Feature]: Pluggable STT backend for macOS Push-to-Talk

question: Should native macOS Push-to-Talk gain a batch STT backend abstraction now, and should the first non-Apple backend route through existing Gateway `tools.media.audio` provider contracts or a new native-only backend contract?
rationale: This cannot safely be resolved as a small code cleanup because it changes native app UX, provider/auth routing, microphone-audio egress, private-network policy, and fallback semantics.

options.title: Design native PTT batch seam first
options.body: Keep Apple Speech as default, add a maintainer-approved batch-only PTT backend boundary, and bridge to existing media-audio/provider contracts where they are the chosen owner boundary.

options.title: Make the broader ASR issue canonical
options.body: Track this slice under https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/46661 if maintainers want one cross-platform native ASR design before macOS PTT work starts.

options.title: Defer native PTT backend routing
options.body: Leave native PTT on Apple Speech until security, UX, and provider ownership requirements are clearer.

recommendation.title: Design native PTT batch seam first
recommendation.body: Keep Apple Speech as default, add a maintainer-approved batch-only PTT backend boundary, and bridge to existing media-audio/provider contracts where they are the chosen owner boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest native macOS voice feature-history signal and is already in the issue timeline for this area.
